title: Credit Scores
objective: After this level you can explain what a credit score measures and what raises or lowers it.
summary: A credit score predicts how likely you are to repay on time, from your credit reports. FICO weighs payment history most, then amounts owed. Income is not part of it, and there is no single score.

cards.headline: Lenders can size you up without ever meeting you.
cards.body: They look at a number built from your borrowing record. Most of these numbers fall between 300 and 850. What goes into one is less mysterious than it seems.

cards.headline: A forecast, not a grade
cards.body: A credit score is a prediction: how likely you are to pay back a loan on time, worked out from the record of your past borrowing in your credit reports. Usually a higher score makes a loan easier to get and may bring a better interest rate. Remember Level 23's barley loans: more risk, higher rate. A score is how a lender estimates the risk.

cards.headline: What's in the recipe
cards.body: FICO scores weigh five things. Paying on time is the biggest single slice, and how much you owe comes next. The length of your credit history, new credit and your mix of credit types fill in the rest. In other words, the score mostly watches what you do with borrowed money.
cards.callout: Payment history 35% · Amounts owed 30% · History length 15% · New credit 10% · Mix 10%

cards.fact: Your salary isn't in your score.
cards.context: A FICO score comes only from your credit report, so income isn't part of it (though lenders may ask about income separately). And you don't have just one score: it varies with the scoring model, the data used and even the day it's calculated.

mascot.line: A common mix-up: your score reads your borrowing record, not your salary.

cards.headline: Credit scores: demystified
learned: A score predicts whether you will repay on time
Payment history counts most, then amounts owed
Income is not in it; there is no single score

questions.prompt: Which single factor carries the most weight in a FICO score?

options.label: Your income
options.rationale: Income isn't in the score at all.

options.label: How long you have had credit

questions.explanation: Payment history is the biggest slice of a FICO score, at 35%.

options.label: The higher earner scores twice as high
options.rationale: Income is not part of the score.

options.label: The higher earner scores a little higher
options.rationale: The score comes only from the credit report, which doesn't include income.

options.label: The lower earner scores higher
options.rationale: Income does not count either way.

options.label: They'd match: income isn't in the score

questions.explanation: A FICO score is calculated only from the credit report. Lenders may ask about income separately, but it is not in the score.

Higher scores come with government subsidies

options.rationale: Rates vary with risk, as in Mesopotamia.
